note: hint-rules-out hits on main as of 2026-10-19 (see scripts/audit-content.mjs for the rule). For the writers: rewrite these hints so they nudge toward the reasoning instead of eliminating wrong options by name.

items.hint: Try each word after "I can". Can you red? Can you tall?
Tree, cup and sand are things. Names of days start with a capital.
Large and huge mean the same as big. Find the opposite.
Blue and softly are not names. Which word names someone at school?
Put each word after "I can". Can you cold? Can you green?
River and stone are things. Which word names a city?
Glad and merry mean the same as happy. Find the opposite.
Bat ends with t and bus ends with s. Check the others.
Dog says woof, cow says moo, hen says cluck.
Run and sit are doing words, and cup is a thing.
Cup ends with p and bus ends with s. Look at the other two.
You cannot eat a chair, a shoe or rain.
Which one can flap its wings, unlike a fish or a cow?
The sun and the rainbow come in the day.
Do we open an umbrella to eat, to sleep, or when water falls?
Stones, sand and smoke are not for drinking.
A spoon, a ball and a pen are not for sleeping.
A shoe, a plate and a chair are not for writing.
It is green, grows in the ground, and is not a car or a book.
A shoe, a broom and a bell are not for eating.
A cloud, a flame and a needle are not for sitting.
Fish cannot live in fire, air or on roads.
A brick, a broom and a boat have no pages.
Count the corners on each shape. A circle has none and a square has 4.
Circle, square and triangle are shapes we draw. Which word is not a shape but a fruit?
Your ears hear and your nose smells. Which body part do you cover so that you cannot see your toys?
Your eyes look and your feet walk. Which body part helps you hear the school bell ring?
"Much" and "Little" go with uncountable nouns; which determiner means the greater part of a group?
"who" and "whom" are for people, and "whose" shows possession.
"many", "several" and "few" go with countable plurals.
"Hey", "Yo" and "Dearest friend" are informal; choose a respectful formal salutation.
A verb is a doing word and an adjective describes. Which one names?
Run is a doing word and school is a place. Which tells a feeling?
A question word starts a question; quietly and green cannot.
Often, sometimes and daily all happen; find the word that means not even once.
Who asks about a person; where asks about a place.
Soon and quick are wrong here. Which word means after the right time?
Do we wear a raincoat to fly or cook, or to keep the rain off?
Sad, angry and tired are different feelings from happy.
Warm and boiling are also hot; find how ice feels.
A baby cat is a kitten and a baby cow is a calf.
A stone, a pillow and a cloud just sit still; which one buzzes all day?
Long, lamp and leaf start like light; find the one that ends like it.
End, stop and finish are opposites of begin.
Packed and filled mean full; which word means nothing inside?
Run is a doing word and blue is a colour; who helps sick people?
"Shut up" and "hey you" are rude. What do we add to ask nicely?
Slow, late and heavy do not mean fast.
Wide and clear are not opposites; find the word for a shut door.
A baby dog is a puppy and a baby hen is a chick.
Huge, wide and tall are big words; find the smallest one.
Cook, coat and kick start like cake; find the one that ends like it.
Begin, start and open are opposites of end.
Close, next and beside all mean near.
A pillow, a cloud and a dream are not places to shop.
Run, soft and quickly are not places; where do you learn?
Plants need water, light and air.
Glad and joyful are twins of happy, not opposites.
Large, huge and giant mean the same as big.
Warm, boiling and spicy are all close to hot.
Above, high and over all point the same way as up.
Packed and crowded mean almost the same as full.
Wide, clear and free are like open; find a door you cannot pass.
Neat, fresh and shiny all mean nearly the same as clean.
Caring, gentle and helpful are twins of kind, not opposites.
Damp, soaked and muddy all have water; find no water at all.
Right, true and exact are twins of correct.
Ancient, used and worn all mean old; find a just-bought bag.
Over, up and high point the same way as above.
Pointed, fine and keen are like sharp; find a worn-down tip.
Tough, tricky and difficult mean nearly the same as hard.
Share, offer and pass are like give; what is the reverse?
Shove, press and nudge are all kinds of push.
Reach, come and enter are like arrive; what do you do at goodbye?
Shiny, clear and glowing are like bright; think of lights off.
Next and early are not opposites; who stands at the end?
Small, new and tiny are not about age.
Pleased, glad and happy are good feelings too; find a bad one.
Run is an action and happy is a feeling; which word is a place?
City and river are common nouns.
Table names a thing, and blue and soft describe; which can you do?
Sky and tree name things, and pretty describes; what do birds do?
Cat is a name and run is an action; which word describes a cat?
Rose is past; rising needs a helping verb.
Sing is an action and bright describes; which one is a place?
Teacher and school are common nouns.
Desk is a noun, and happy and green describe; which word is an action?
Song and stage are things, and loud describes; what do children do with a song?
Dog is a name and bark is an action; which word describes a dog?
Ran is a verb; quickly tells how.
Two and many need more than one orange; pick the article for one.
Watch/watches are present forms.
Angry is a bad feeling; tiny and slow are not feelings.
Small means the opposite size; quiet and soft are not sizes.
Slow and sleepy mean taking a long time.
End and finish are not twins of begin.
A kind person helps and shares, not rude or mean.
Wrong and false are opposites of correct; broken is not about answers.
A careful person thinks before acting, not hasty or wild.
Ignore, hide and cover mean not using your eyes.
Thin means not wide or thick.
People build a home for a horse with stalls and hay. Hive, sty and nest are for other animals.
A farmer keeps pigs in a muddy pen. Stable, kennel and hive belong to other animals.
Lemon is sour, karela is bitter, salt is salty. Which food do bees make?
You did not taste, smell or hear the hot cup. Your hand felt the heat. Which sense was that?
Your nose can find burnt toast, ripe mango and soap. Which thing can only be found by looking?
Garbage, smoke and rotten eggs smell bad. Which one is a flower we put in garlands?
A prince and a princess are children; what do we call a king's wife?
Delhi, Raju and Sunday all start with capitals — which word could be any one of many?
Slow, late and lazy are the opposite of a cheetah; find the word that means the same.
Huge and tall are the opposite; find the word that also describes an ant.
Cot, cut and cap start like "cat", but rhymes must share the ending sound.
"blue" is a colour; you need the past form of "blow", which sounds the same.
A triangle has 3 sides, 3 angles and a closed boundary.
Acute is less than 90° and obtuse is more than 90°. What is the name for exactly 90°?
Ser, maund and tola are old weights. Which old unit measures length along your forearm?
A kilogram is 1,000 g. Which is heavier: that, or 800 g, 900 g and 950 g?
Carbohydrates are the starchy energy foods. Egg, fish and paneer are body-building foods. Which is starchy?
A brick and an eraser keep their shape; air spreads everywhere. Which one takes the shape of its cup?
Honey, coconut oil and vinegar can be poured and flow. Which one is made of hard little crystals?
Jar Y's juice has a flat top and jar Z's dots fill the jar. Which jar holds something that keeps its own shape?
Coconut water and rain water flow, and air spreads out. Which one is hard and keeps its shape?
Brick, pencil and plate keep their shape. Which one can be poured from a jar, even if slowly?
Plants wilt and animals get thirsty without it. Gold, toys and plastic are not needed to live.
Which word could fill "a ___ of birds" — unlike a river or a city like Mumbai?
Ask which word names a quality of a good person, like kindness or courage — not a table or a crowd.
A mouse and a snail are timid or slow; which animal is called king of the jungle?
A bakery has bread and a museum has old objects — where would you get a borrowing card?
"Your buddy" and "See ya" are casual; pick the formal closing used for an unknown reader.
"Hey!" and "Yo, Principal!" are too casual, and "Dear Diary" is not for a person.
Non-renewable means it took millions of years to form and runs out. Sunlight, wind and rivers keep coming back.
Clear glass and clean water let you see through them sharply. Opaque blocks light; translucent gives a blurry view.
A window pane must let light through so you can see outside clearly. Wood, cardboard and rubber block light.
A plug cover must stop current reaching your fingers. Copper, aluminium and iron are metals that conduct.
Germination is sprouting and photosynthesis is food-making. Which term means seeds spreading to new places?
Dispersal is seeds travelling; pollination happens in flowers. Which word means a seed sprouting into a young plant?
Maize, wheat and rice grains stay in one piece when soaked. Which seed splits into two halves?
Seeds travel by wind, water, animals or bursting pods. Which word is about leaves making food instead?
"and" adds, "but" contrasts, "or" gives a choice; which conjunction gives a reason?
When two nouns make one single item, use a singular verb, not are or were.
"many", "few" and "several" go with countable nouns.
"because" gives a reason and "therefore" a result; which shows an opposite idea?
An author writes and a passenger travels; recall Uncle Raju at the vegetable stall.
End, pause and cancel do not mean starting.
Entry and welcome are about coming in; find the word about going away.
"morale" means team spirit and "mural" is a wall painting; which word is a story's lesson?
Acute is less than 90° and obtuse is more. Name the square-corner angle of exactly 90°.
A ruler measures length and a compass draws circles. Which instrument has a half-circle marked in degrees for angles?
"but" contrasts, "nor" is negative; pick a coordinating word that simply adds erasers.
A long speech or a heavy meal is not about seeing; a glimpse is brief.
A mural is a wall painting and mortal means must die; which word is a story's lesson?
Adopt and repair mean keeping or caring for something — find the opposite idea.
Careless and late are the opposite of diligent.
Tiny and narrow are opposites of vast.
Slow and late are opposites of rapid.
Proteins break into amino acids and starch into glucose. Which two products do fats give after digestion?
Nucleus, membrane and mitochondria occur in both cell types. Which rigid outer layer do only plant cells have?
Haemoglobin is in blood and melanin in skin. Which pigment makes leaves green and traps light in chloroplasts?
Earthworm, mushroom and Hydra are built of many cells. Which organism moves by pseudopodia as a single cell?
Amoeba moves by pushing out temporary bulges of its cytoplasm. Cilia and flagella are permanent hair-like structures.
No nuclear membrane means a prokaryote. Amoeba, Paramecium and yeast are eukaryotes. Which is prokaryotic?
The cell wall is fully permeable in plants; the nucleus controls activities. Which thin layer decides what passes in and out?
Paramecium, Chlamydomonas and yeast are single-celled. Which organism has tentacles and a body made of many cells?
The SI unit of force honours the scientist who gave the laws of motion. Pascal is for pressure and joule for energy.
Friction, muscular force and the normal force from a table all need touching. Which force acts from a distance?
A thermometer reads temperature and a barometer reads air pressure. Which device stretches a spring to read force?
Sodium and aluminium are solids, and bromine is a liquid non-metal. Which metal flows like silver water in old thermometers?
A temple bell rings when struck. Malleability is about sheets and ductility about wires. Which property is about sound?
This non-metal catches fire on its own in air, so it is kept under water. Sulphur, carbon and iodine are safe in air.
Malleability is about sheets, sonority about ringing, lustre about shine. Which property is about wires?
Recall the reactivity series. Copper and gold do not react with water, and iron only slowly. Which reacts violently?
Zinc, mercury and aluminium are metals. Which choice is a black solid found in coal and graphite?
"Many", "Few" and "Several" go with countable plural nouns.
"Prefer" has its own fixed preposition, different from "rather than".
"visible" is for seeing and "legible" for reading; which one is for hearing?
"concise", "vivid" and "witty" are good qualities that would not bore anyone.
"peek" is a quick look and "pique" means to stir interest.
"eager" and "joyful" are opposites; which choice means not willing?
Century = 100; millennium = 1000.
"blurry", "mute" and "lazy" would make an account useless.
A vector quantity can point backwards along a line. Distance, speed and time intervals cannot be negative.
